articles.title: Tuchanka: Turian Platoon - Mass Effect 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Tuchanka: Turian Platoon Side Mission, including where to find all the items, how to survive
articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about the Tuchanka: Turian Platoon Side Mission, including where to find all the items, how to survive all the combat encounters, and how to make the right choices for your playthrough.

While this Side Mission doesn't expire at all, the one that follows it, " Tuchanka: Bomb ", DOES. "Bomb" expires three Missions after you complete "Turian Platoon", so if you want very unique dialogue opportunities in "Bomb", delay "Turian Platoon" as well.

Looking for something specific? Click the links below to jump to...

Weapons: M-9 Tempest Phaeston (if not acquired in " Omega: Aria T'Loak ")

Phaeston (if not acquired in " Omega: Aria T'Loak ")

Prerequisite: Complete " Priority: Sur'Kesh "

Location: Krogan DMZ - Aralakh - Tuchanka

This Side Mission is unlocked after you complete " Priority: Sur'Kesh ". Once you've done so, then in the aftermath cutscene you'll be asked to meet with Primarch Victus regarding a sensitive matter. Turns out the Turians have lost a platoon on Tuchanka, one lead by Victus' son.

Tuchanka is one of the main worlds for this leg of the game's story, so its system, Krogan DMZ, will be marked with a flashing white on the Galaxy Map. You'll be dropped off in the Aralakh system, and Tuchanka will be the third planet here.

You may have a few spots on Tuchanka you can land on: you'll want to pick the spot labeled "Downed Vessel" But while you're here, you may want to consider getting the following Search and Rescue items from the Krogan DMZ's other systems (although Nith is admittedly optional since it only contains Fuel):

Squad Tactics: James is a fantastic choice for his armor-stripping powers: Incendiary Ammo and Carnage. Garrus is also a good choice for his Armor-Piercing Ammo.

James is a fantastic choice for his armor-stripping powers: Incendiary Ammo and Carnage.

Garrus is also a good choice for his Armor-Piercing Ammo.

Unique Dialogue: Garrus gives the most unique dialogue for this Side Mission. If you don't have Garrus, pick James . EDI provides some alternate dialogue for the start of this Mission. The Side Mission after this one, " Tuchanka: Bomb ", has some very unique dialogue. However "Bomb" expires three Missions after unlocking you complete "Turian Platoon" (with drastic consequences), so if you want this unique dialogue you should delay "Turian Platoon" in order to make that easier on you. You'll want to wait until after " Priority: The Citadel 2 " and / or " Priority: Rannoch ".

Garrus gives the most unique dialogue for this Side Mission. If you don't have Garrus, pick James .

EDI provides some alternate dialogue for the start of this Mission.

The Side Mission after this one, " Tuchanka: Bomb ", has some very unique dialogue. However "Bomb" expires three Missions after unlocking you complete "Turian Platoon" (with drastic consequences), so if you want this unique dialogue you should delay "Turian Platoon" in order to make that easier on you. You'll want to wait until after " Priority: The Citadel 2 " and / or " Priority: Rannoch ".

Shepard's Loadout: This level is primarily made up of tight, enclosed spaces, so bringing a Sniper Rifle is just added weight. Instead, focus on short and medium-range weapons like SMGs, shotguns and assault rifles.

This level is primarily made up of tight, enclosed spaces, so bringing a Sniper Rifle is just added weight. Instead, focus on short and medium-range weapons like SMGs, shotguns and assault rifles.

For those playing the original release of Mass Effect 3 on Xbox 360, PS3 or PC, there's a bug in this Side Mission relating to the Harvesters you fight. If you kill either of the first two Harvesters, then the fourth that shows up at the end will never appear, soft-locking the Mission. If you accidentally do that, use the Restart Mission save file from the Load Screen to try again. Legendary Edition and Wii U Special Edition players don't have to worry: this bug was fixed for those versions.

Unfortunately, due to the bad terrain Cortez isn't able to land anywhere near the crashed Turian frigate, but it does bring one unintended bonus: you're far back enough that the Reaper forces will be unaware of your presence! After landing, Shepard will get Victus' rough position with a signal flare, and the Side Mission begins.

SMG Magazine Upgrade - From the start of the level the path will turn right towards a ladder. Instead of doing that, turn left to find this in the rubble.

Spare Parts - 3,125 credits. From the SMG Magazine Upgrade described above, climb up the ladder and press on through the rubble. Ahead you'll encounter three squatting Husks: kill them quick as you can, then investigate the debris they were squatting in front of for credits.

M-9 Tempest - From the Spare Parts described above, climb up the ladder to find a crashed escape pod with three dead Turians in front of it. Jump across the gap, then check the Turians to find this new weapon.

When you vault over the fallen column ahead on the left, you'll get into a cutscene where Shepard spots some Cannibals up ahead, unaware of your presence. After it's over, press forward and exploit this golden preemptive strike opportunity and neutralize the threats before they notice you. Then, a Harvester shows up.

If you're playing the original release of the game on Xbox 360, PS3 or PC (but not Wii U), killing this first Harvester will cause the final one at the end of the level to not spawn in, soft-locking the Mission! If you do kill it, load the Restart Mission file in the Load Menu.

This bug is NOT present in the Legendary Edition.

The Harvester is a very formidable foe, and demands the utmost respect on the battlefield.

Their main cannons deal huge area, so make sure you're in cover at all times and spread your squad out to minimize splash damage casualties. Infiltrators can work around this issue by using Tactical Cloak, letting them snipe as they please.

Harvesters always keep their distance, sometimes to the point that you can never get up close to them, so you won't have to worry about any melee attacks.

It's very hard to take out Harvesters whilst under enemy fire, so make sure you take out all other enemies before focusing on the Harvester itself.

The only bar a Harvester has is Armor, so use Incendiary / Armor-Piercing Ammo, Incinerate and Carnage to take chunks out of it.

The Harvester is also part of a mechanic unique to this level in particular:

The Harvester will start firing on the Escape Pod, weakening its health and gradually killing the pair of turians at each pod.

You can distract the Harvester by firing at it, where it will attack you instead of the Escape Pod. If you leave it along for too long, however, it will turn its attention back to the Escape Pod.

You DO NOT need to kill the Harvester! It'll fly away once you've taken out half its Armor.

Once the Harvester is down, any surviving Turians will thank you and let you know of another pod just up ahead. To continue, check the right-hand wall for a ladder to climb up.

Sniper Rifle Spare Ammo - When you climb to the top of the ladder, STOP! Look left to find this mod on some rubble.

Spare Parts - 6,250 credits. From the Sniper Rifle Spare Ammo described above, go down the drop up ahead to find a turian body. Continue past him and then look right to find this pile of Spare Parts.

Phaeston - From the Spare Parts described above, return to the dead turian and then go left. Ahead will be a dead Turian with this gun next to him. NOTE: This will not be present if you already picked up a Phaeston during the Omega DLC .

SMG Ultralight Materials - From the Phaeston described above, head forward into the dark noon and turn left to spot this mod under the rubble.

Med Kit - 50 XP. When you drop down the next ladder, directly ahead will be a stone column leaning on the right-hand wall. Check behind the column for this Med Kit.

If you're playing the original release of the game on Xbox 360, PS3 or PC (but not Wii U), killing the second Harvester up ahead will cause the final one at the end of the level to not spawn in, soft-locking the Mission! If you do kill it, load the Restart Mission file in the Load Menu.

Again, this bug is NOT present in the Legendary Edition.

The next area of conflict features all of the enemies, including a Marauder and another Harvester. Take them all down quickly and drive the Harvester away to save the Turians (that'll happen with about 1/3rd of its Armor left). Once the area is good and quiet, head right and down the drop to continue.

Hahne-Kedar Chestplate - After the drop, turn right and vault over the fallen column. This will be sitting on a ledge to your left.

Flight Recorder - From the Hahne-Kedar Chestplate described above, drop down the hole in the ground ahead. You'll see a Datapad up ahead near some rubble, giving you a bit of insight into how the men feel about Victus' leadership.

Shotgun Smart Choke - From the Flight Recorder described above, turn left to spot this on some rubble in the corner ahead.

Junk - 3,125 credits. From the Shotgun Smart Choke described above, turn right and a trio of Husks will be dropped in right in front of you. Mow them down, then check the body of the Turian where the Husks dropped in. Make sure to grab this before dropping down the next ladder!

Resistance ramps up when another Harvester appears, but fortunately it retreats with about a sliver of its health left. You should try and do this where the Harvester first appears at the top of the ramp: driving it away now will prevent it from flying down the ramp and spawning a LOT more Reaper enemies for you to deal with.

Press forward and move downhill through the collapsed ruins: at the bottom you'll finally spot the crashed Turian ship Lieutenant Victus commanded. From there, the path turns right.

Med Kit - After dropping down a short ledge, check the right-hand wall for this Med Kit.

Sniper Rifle Extended Barrel - From the Med Kit described above, drop down the second, much higher ledge, then look left to spot this mod.After scaring off the third Harvester, continue down to find this along the path.

The next area becomes a crucial chokepoint, where a Brute is thrown at your squad along with a bevy of Cannibals and Marauders. There is a Reaper Blackstar available at the base of a column across from the entry point if you're having difficulty with the Brute: it's powerful enough to one-shot it on any difficulty! But you may also want to save it for the Harvester, who'll bookend the encounter.

Once the Harvester and any Reaper stragglers are dead, you’ll meet up with Lt. Victus, who'll explain how exactly his team managed to get pinned down by Reapers. Here, you can pick...

"Bad calls happen" for +2 Paragon Points .

After this, the Lieutenant reveals the exact reason why they came on Tuchanka: a bomb in Cerberus' possession that the Turians were sent to deactivate, which is now in Cerberus' possession. Unfortunately Lt. Victus' men are low on spirit and he'd prefer to abandon the mission, so you'll have to motivate them with...

"Appeal to their honor" for +2 Paragon Points .

"Kick their asses!" for +2 Renegade Points .

Either choice will be successful, and Shepard will return to the Normandy.

Shepard chats with Hackett, and both agree that something isn't right about Cerberus just happening to have a bomb on Tuchanka. After the call is over, Shepard approaches Primarch Victus, who remains tight-lipped about the situation and asks if Shepard would give up information that puts Earth at risk. Here, you can answer...

"Yes. I have to trust you" for +2 Paragon Points .

"No. Earth comes first" for +2 Renegade Points .

Unfortunately neither appeal to him. Hopefully you can learn more when you reunite with the Primarch's son back on Tuchanka.

If this was the first main Mission you completed after " Priority: Sur'Kesh ", you'll now be approached by your STG Doctor saying he's developed a cure. You can get up to +4 Paragon Points or +4 Renegade Points depending on your choices, and unlock " Priority: Tuchanka " too! You still have total freedom to ignore it, however.

After the cutscenes, do another sweep of the Normandy:

CIC - Chat with the Primarch again, your Krogan Leader, Traynor, Joker, and EDI.

Crew Deck - Chat with Garrus and Liara in Port Observation (with an extra discussion when you open the door to leave).

Engineering - Pop by Javik's place for a few comments. Gabby and Ken will have an exchange, and Allers has a news recording you can overhear. If you completed this Side Mission after " Priority: Rannoch ", then you may be able to overhear an exchange between Tali and EDI as well.

If you completed this Side Mission after " Priority: Rannoch ", then you may be able to overhear an exchange between Tali and EDI as well.

Shuttle Bay - Chat with James for a very small comment.

articles.title: Citadel Excursion 2 - Mass Effect 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about exploring the Citadel in the opening act of the game, just before you do "Priority:
articles.body:
This page of IGN's Mass Effect 3 wiki guide is all about exploring the Citadel in the opening act of the game, just before you do " Priority: Tuchanka ". Here we'll guide you to all the various Side Missions you'll hand in and character interactions you can fulfill.

The purpose of this page is to make sure you've completed all possible interactions before you do " Priority: Tuchanka ". Completing that Mission will refresh the Citadel, and many character interactions and Side Missions will be replaced with new ones. As such, there are a few notes we'd like to make first:

We highly recommend that you first go through the Citadel Excursion 1 page and make sure you've done all the major interactions in it , if you haven't already. You'll pick up a great many Side Missions that you'll be able to hand in at this point.

This page expects that you've done " Attican Traverse: Krogan Team ", " N7: Cerberus Abductions " and " N7: Cerberus Attack " - All of these have items that you'll hand in on this page to complete Side Missions. We also expect that you've picked up the " Citadel: GX12 Thermal Pipe " Side Mission from Engineer Adams.

We also expect you to complete the Search and Rescue section below - This is again because you'll get items that you'll hand in to complete Side Missions here. The Ismar Frontier cluster unlocks by picking up the " Ismar Frontier: Prototype Components " Side Mission at Huerta Memorial Hospital.

Finally, we assume you've kept up with Steve Cortez's personal storyline , where he's emotionally ready to say goodbye to his husband Robert.

Before we start with exploring the Citadel, you should complete the Search and Rescue table below to get Credits and Quest Items for Side Missions that you'll be handing in further down the page.

The Ismar Frontier requires you to pick up the " Ismar Frontier: Prototype Components " Side Mission at Huerta Memorial Hospital.

The Vular system in Kite's Nest requires you to negotiate with the black market seller on the Citadel rather than kill General Oraka in " Aria: Blue Suns ". The only item there is that Side Mission's quest item, so if you opted to kill General Oraka, you're not missing out on anything (unless you really like the planet descriptions).

Head through the security walls and then turn left to find Cortez at the memorial area. Talk to him to continue his storyline and get +2 Reputation .

There's a Paragon Interrupt during this scene, but you get no Morality Points for using it.

Head into Cargo Hold: C and talk to the Batarian Preacher to hand in " Kite's Nest: Pillars of Strength ", which will give you 15,000 Credits, +5 Reputation and bolsters the Batarian Fleet War Asset. If you didn't get it, you can find it on Khar'shan, the second planet in the Harsa system in the Kite's Nest cluster.

Go to Cargo Hold: B and talk to Kelly Chambers to catch up with her. If you've been following this guide correctly, then in this scene she'll confess that she sent reports about you to the Illusive Man as part of her job in Mass Effect 2. At this, you can say...

"You did what?" for +2 Renegade Points , which severely traumatizes Kelly.

Exit the elevator and go left to find Dominic Osoba at the window. If you found the Dog Tags of his son during " N7: Cerberus Abductions ", you can hand them in here to complete " Benning: Evidence " for +5 Reputation and 90 XP. If you missed them, you can buy them at Spectre Requisitions .

Head to Udina's office to catch this easily-missed conversation where he discusses your Virmire Survivor accepting the position of Spectre. Here you can reply...

"Good for her / him" for +2 Paragon Points .

"This won't end well" for +2 Renegade Points .

None of his Investigate topics have updated dialogue, unfortunately.

If Dr. Michel isn't aboard the Normandy, you can check in with her in the corner of the first room to learn about the current condition of your Virmire Survivor.

Now head inside and talk to the Virmire Survivor themselves about accepting the position of Spectre, and how they're feeling. Aside from giving you +2 Reputation , this meeting is again important in helping your Virmire Survivor reconcile with Shepard later.

Head through the door opposite the room your Virmire Survivor is in to hand in " Ismar Frontier: Prototype Components " for 90 XP. If you didn't grab them, you can find them by scanning Metaponto, the fourth planet in the Aquila system in the Ismar Frontier cluster.

From the elevator, head left and up the stairs to talk to Barla Von behind the far desk to cash in " Citadel: Barla Von ", giving you 120 XP and +5 Reputation . If you didn't pick up the Shadow Broker Wet Squad that Barla Von is looking for, you can find them by scanning Rothla, the fourth planet in the Dranek system of the Krogan DMZ .

At Barla Von's post, access the Elkoss Combine Arsenal Supplies store and buy the GX12 Thermal Pipe (called "E-Gel Thermal Conduit" in in the storefront itself, for some reason) for 1,000 credits, progressing the " Citadel: GX12 Thermal Pipe " Side Mission for Engineer Adams. It's quite cheap, so don't feel bad about buying it without the full 10% discount.

In the Apollo's Cafe area you can find Matriarch Aethyta serving drinks, who Mass Effect 2 players may recognize from Illium . Talk to her and you'll begin a very interesting conversation. When she mentions keeping an eye on Liara, say...

"You should talk" for +2 Paragon Points .

"You shouldn't spy on her" for +2 Renegade Points .

During this conversation a Paragon Interrupt will pop up: pull it for +5 Paragon Points . A Renegade Interrupt will also appear here: pull that for +5 Renegade Points .

After this, find Liara at the balcony and talk to her. If you pick "[Make her talk to her]", the strength of the Asari Second Fleet will be increased by 25 TMS.

You can then head back to the cafe bar and hear a 10-part conversation between Liara and Aethyta that will be very interesting for those who played the first Mass Effect. To move to the next part of this conversation, walk to one of the nearby staircases and then walk back to them.

Now go to the lowest balcony with the two stores and talk to Ereba at the Nos Astra Sporting Goods storefront, which will complete " Citadel: Krogan Dying Message ". You MUST have picked it up during " Attican Traverse: Krogan Team ", otherwise this Side Mission cannot be started, let alone completed.

Handing in the message will give you +5 Reputation and 90 XP.

If you went the Paragon route with the " Aria: Blue Suns " Side Mission and talked to Krannik, you should now head upstairs to the Cipritine Armory kiosk and talk to Kannik to continue that Side Mission (if you had General Oraka killed, click here to skip to the next section of this page ).

This will have you hand in Black Market Artifacts, appeasing Krannik into giving General Oraka the black market weapons he's asking for, netting you 210 XP, 5,000 credits, and bolstering the Terminus Fleet by +50 TMS. If you don't have the Black Market Artifacts, you can find them by scanning Vana, the third planet in the Vular system of the Kite's Nest cluster.

With Kannik appeased, return to General Oraka at the bottom of the steps just across from Apollo's Cafe. Talk to him to conclude the Side Mission for +5 Paragon Points .

In the exterior area of Purgatory, talk with the human woman in the dress at the railing just outside the entrance door to conclude " Citadel: Improved Power Grid " for +5 Reputation , 30 XP, 1,000 Credits and strengthening the Alliance Fifth Fleet by 8 TMS.

If you missed the power grid schematics from the " N7: Cerberus Attack " Side Mission, you can buy them from Spectre Requisitions for 1,000 credits.

If you completed " Aria: Eclipse ", " Aria: Blue Suns " and " Aria: Blood Pack ", you can talk to Aria again to get her reactions to fulfilling her requests. You can ask her about your new task force, as well as about each individual mercenary gang.

With the Citadel now completely done for now, here's what you can do on the Normandy:

CIC - Check your Private Terminal to read an email from Cortez, which gives you 375 XP and the Rogue Fighter Pilots War Asset, worth 20 TMS.

Crew Deck - Swing by Liara's Intel terminal for the Intel you picked up. You should have the following: Weapon Upgrade Kit - +5% Ammo Capacity or +5% Weapon Damage. Advanced Biotic Implants - +5% Power Damage or +5% Power Recharge Speed.

Weapon Upgrade Kit - +5% Ammo Capacity or +5% Weapon Damage.

Advanced Biotic Implants - +5% Power Damage or +5% Power Recharge Speed.

Engineering - Talk to Engineer Adams, as well as Gabby if present, to progress " Citadel: GX12 Thermal Pipe ".

Shuttle Bay - Lastly, talk to Cortez for some post-memorial thoughts.

articles.title: Take-Two Boss Strauss Zelnick on GTA 6 Expectations, GTA Online, and the Decade to Come
articles.summary: IGN interviews Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick 10 days before the biggest release in entertainment history: GTA 6.
articles.body:
10 days out from the release of GTA 6 , Strauss Zelnick tells me he’s feeling “optimistic.” It might be the understatement of the century. Reporting its second quarter fiscal year 2027 results tonight, Take-Two said preorders for Rockstar’s next game are tracking “far in excess” of the company’s initial expectations. “We know that the numbers will speak for themselves soon enough,” the Rockstar parent company added.

Or, as Zelnick put it to me during a phone interview, “I'm looking forward to the launch.”

GTA 6 is expected to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time, surpassing any movie or video game before it in terms of sales and money made. There are concerns it might not just crash the PlayStation Store, but jam up the internet, given so many millions across the world are expected to download the whopping 212GB that make up Rockstar’s surefire hit.

Still, GTA 6, like all video games these days, is beset by threats from all sides. The recent explosion in AI-fueled game clones and PS5 jailbreaks has raised the chances of GTA 6 turning up on PC before Rockstar has had a chance to release it officially. But what can Take-Two do about it?

Meanwhile, all eyes are on Rockstar to see what happens after GTA 6 comes out, after its developers recently insisted its next game won’t take another eight years to make . Yes, it really has been eight years since Red Dead Redemption 2 came out.

In the interview below, we touch on all these topics and more, joke about yet another potential GTA 6 delay, and learn that GTA 6 is so popular it might have even caused sales of Take-Two’s own NBA 2K27 to miss expectations .

IGN: Finally, after a decade of development, delays, ups and downs, GTA 6 is coming out. I'm just wondering, Strauss, how does it feel right now?

Strauss Zelnick: Optimistic. I'm looking forward to the launch.

IGN: Normally I'd ask you if you if there was a risk of GTA 6 being delayed. I've had conversations with you in the past that I'm guessing you can be pretty confident this time it's not going to be delayed again.

Strauss Zelnick: It’s not going to be delayed again.

IGN: There's a line in the financials about Rockstar continuing to support GTA Online with new content and ongoing events for its vast community. I'm just curious what impact you forecast GTA 6 having on GTA Online when the game comes out? What are your expectations about GTA Online from next week onwards?

Strauss Zelnick: We intend to keep supporting GTA Online and it has been very successful. It's been very resilient. It has continued to grow over the years, so we feel very good about it.

IGN: There's another line about preorders for GTA 6 tracking far in excess of your expectations, and you say the numbers will speak for themselves soon enough. Do you make any preparations to try and ensure a smooth launch for your customers? Is GTA 6 so big you might actually crash the internet? Do you do anything around that to try and prevent any problems there?

Strauss Zelnick: We are very focused on that and we intend to do the very best we can to have a smooth delivery experience for all of our customers.

Hannah Sage (EVP, Finance and Chief Accounting Officer): And the preload starts tomorrow in an effort to minimize that impact.

IGN: There was a very interesting recent interview of senior Rockstar developers in Bloomberg. They said the foundation was laid for faster development following GTA 6. I was wondering what your expectation is now with Rockstar? Do you believe Rockstar will be able to release more games faster than before? Will you continue to treat Rockstar as you have done with GTA 6, with the budget and giving them the time needed to create the game like this? What's your take?

Strauss Zelnick: I certainly will continue to support all of our labels in their quest to make the best entertainment experiences on earth. And each of our three labels has its own bespoke strategy and approach and I'm supportive of that.

We do think that the nature and velocity of the content we'll see from our iconic franchises, including GTA, will look dramatically different over the next decade. And that's really being driven by our industry leading commitment to releasing the highest quality entertainment, to reaching our players in new ways and in new places and trying to maintain engagement with our consumers post-launch.

IGN: We've seen hackers using AI to clone games much faster than ever before, even try to jailbreak consoles. And there is some concern about this leading to potentially GTA 6 being made available on PC unofficially or places that you aren't releasing it. I was just wondering how much of a threat this is to your business? And, is there anything meaningful you can do about it?

Strauss Zelnick: I don't think it’s a financial matter, in terms of a threat to our business. I do think it’s a creative matter. It's important to everyone, our developers and our consumers alike, to deliver the experience Rockstar envisions. And at the same time, of course, we protect our intellectual property vigilantly. So we are focused on these concerns. We're not in the least cavalier about them. Technology is advancing quickly. And at the same time, I do think that pretty much everyone wants the Rockstar experience as Rockstar intended.

IGN: Related, last week Anthropic confirmed they took steps to block Claude from reverse engineering video games. I would assume you would welcome that. And would you like to see other AI companies like OpenAI do the same thing to prevent people from using these powerful AI models to clone your games?

Strauss Zelnick: I think all companies should be protecting intellectual property, their own and everyone else's. And if you're in the intellectual property business, which Anthropic is and OpenAI is, then it seems ironic on the one hand to stomp on someone else's IP and hope that yours is protected.

IGN: Your financials mention that NBA 2K27 came in below your forecast. What do you put that down to and how do you improve upon matters?

Strauss Zelnick: I think the key point is that while below our forecast, NBA 2K27 is our second best release of NBA 2K in history. It's an immensely successful title. It sold 4 million units. And in launching more content than ever before for the rest of the year, we have expectations that the title will do even better than it already has done.

I do think that this timing may have affected performance so far. It has been a crowded period, and we do think that GTA 6 coming has had an influence on the consumer. That said, we're thrilled with how NBA 2K27 is performing.

IGN: There's also a line there about Borderlands 4. It's now sold over 100 million units as a franchise. Congratulations for that. But there's a line about what lies ahead for this series. Is it your belief that Borderlands can meaningfully grow its audience and improve commercially? And if so, from your point of view, how can it achieve that?

Strauss Zelnick: The answer is yes. It is a big hit franchise already and I think there's plenty more to come. I think if you ask the team at Gearbox, they are highly optimistic that there's a lot yet to be done and I do believe that there is a lot yet to be done. I'm very excited going forward about all things Borderlands.

Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

articles.title: All Magic Bean and Soft Soil Locations - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Welcome to IGN's guide to All Magic Bean Soil Locations. Magic Bean Soil plots are spread all throughout the world of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
articles.body:
Welcome to IGN's guide to All Magic Bean Soil Locations . Magic Bean Soil plots are spread all throughout the world of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake and look like small anthills with an opening at the top. Planting a Magic Bean in the soil as Young Link will cause a Magic Platform to appear in Adult Link's time, leading you to a Reward. There are 10 Magic Bean Soil locations total, and each one also houses a Gold Skulltula that can be freed by releasing a Bug nearby. We have checklists for each of those bug-released Skulltulas as well as checklists for the loot you can get as an adult using the Bean platforms.

See IGN's full guide to Magic Bean Soil below:

First, let's quickly cover how to get Magic Beans. Magic Beans can be purchased from the Bean Seller in Zora River, accessible once you have the Bombs. He sells you 1 Magic Bean at a time, and the price increases by 10 Rupees each time. He sells out after 10 Magic Beans, exactly enough to fill all plots.

Below is a list of all 10 Magic Bean Soil plots. All of these are accessible as Young Link, though the final two require you to become Adult Link first then go back.

Location : Just past the front entrance of Zora River from Hyrule Field. Find it right next to the Bean Seller.

Reward : Access to the high platform in the middle of the Zora River (also accessible by using a Cucco). 1 Skulltula (using a bug in a bottle).

Location : Located behind the Kokiri Forest Item Shop.

Reward : Access to a high platform above the Kokiri Shop that holds a Purple Rupee. 1 Skulltula (using a bug in a bottle).

Location : From the Lost Woods entrance, go left, then left . The soil is near the entryway.

Reward : Access to a treasure chest on a high platform that has a Purple Rupee inside. 1 Skulltula (using a bug in a bottle).

Location : Found in the same room as the Forest Stage grotto. From the Lost Woods entrance, go right, left, right, left, then left . Find the soil on the right side of the room behind the Business Scrub.

Reward : 2 Gold Skulltulas (including one Skulltula using a bug in a bottle).

Location : Found under the large tree on the north side of the Graveyard in Kakariko Village (nearest what becomes Dampe's grave as Adult Link).

Reward : 1 Piece of Heart. 1 Skulltula (using a bug in a bottle).

Location : Found right next to the entrance to Dodongo's Cavern in Death Mountain.

articles.title: Skydance Games Confirms Layoffs Following Warner Bros.-Paramount Merger
articles.summary: Skydance Games has laid off staff following last month's Warner Bros-Paramount merger.
articles.body:
Skydance Games has laid off staff following last month's Warner Bros-Paramount merger.

Rumblings of a restructuring started when employees from the recently established Paramount Games Studio reported they had been let go earlier today. Skydance confirmed the layoffs in a statement shared with Variety .

"As part of our ongoing efforts to position Skydance Games for long-term growth and success, we are implementing reorganization and operational shifts across a few areas of our business," a Skydance spokesperson said. "We have stepped back and taken some time to consider where we are investing our efforts and have made the difficult decision to scale down some of our projects.

"As a result, there are roles impacted. This is not a reflection of the talent, dedication, or creativity of those affected and we are grateful for their contributions. We are committed to approaching the process with transparency, care and respect for those who are leaving the company."

Paramount Games – which encompasses gaming studios like Skydance Interactive, Skydance New Media, and other Paramount and Skydance entities – was announced this past June. During an interview with IGN at the time , senior vice president, head of creative and production Shawn Kittelsen detailed what was then described as a renewed push into AAA gaming. This included the announcement of Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin , as well as games based on projects like Yellowstone, Tulsa King, and Lioness .

Now, many of the people who would have been or were working on projects in its upcoming slate have been laid off. Writer Mallory Dobry , senior concept artist Ameorry Luo , lead VFX artist Michael Parsons , and associate design director David Ballard were just a few of the names impacted by the move, with each taking to LinkedIn to update their work status.

"Skydance just lost a ton of great talent yesterday," lead engineer David Vera said . "I was not affected this time, but so many passionate, hard-working, talented individuals are now competing with thousands of others trying to get their next gig. In this tumultuous climate, it's hard to find great talent and collaborators to help build your next team and game. The Skydance crew wasn't let go because of performance or problematic behaviors. These are all extremely worthy folks who were pushing themselves to the limit to try to make something they could all be proud of."

Insider Gaming reported that at least 30 developers were affected by Skydance layoffs, adding that "it's believed that the real number is higher." The Skydance games layoffs arrive in a post-Warner Bros.-Paramount merger world. The two entertainment giants were given the go-ahead to join under one Skydance banner last month. We've felt the ramifications of that deal in more ways than one today, as DC Studios just announced that James Gunn and Peter Safran would be stepping down as co-chairmen of the company , effective December 1.

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

articles.title: GTA 6 Caused Some Gamers to Hold Off on Buying New Games — Including Take-Two's Own NBA 2K27, Strauss Zelnick Says
articles.summary: The behemoth that is GTA 6 looms large over the video game industry, and it’s so big that it not only caused the September crush of releases, but caused some gamers to hold off on buying new games entirely.
articles.body:
The behemoth that is GTA 6 looms large over the video game industry, and it’s so big that it not only caused the September crush of releases, but caused some gamers to hold off on buying new games.

Reporting its latest financial results, Take-Two, parent company of GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games, said that its own NBA 2K27 had sold 4 million units, which was “below our forecast for the period.”

Take-Two, which owns both 2K and NBA developer Visual Concepts, said that the NBA 2K27 launch window was “unusually busy, with numerous entertainment experiences competing for players’ attention.” In an accompanying interview with IGN , Zelnick expanded on the point, adding that he felt that GTA 6 had an impact also.

“I think the key point is that while below our forecast, NBA 2K27 is our second best release of NBA 2K in history. It's an immensely successful title. It sold 4 million units. And in launching more content than ever before for the rest of the year, we have expectations that the title will do even better than it already has done,” Zelnick began.

“I do think that this timing may have affected performance so far. It has been a crowded period, and we do think that GTA 6 coming has had an influence on the consumer. That said, we're thrilled with how NBA 2K27 is performing.”

GTA 6 is credited with forcing developers and publishers to either bring their releases forward or move them back in an effort to avoid November. The likes of The Blood of Dawn Walker, Onimusha: Way of the Sword, Marvel's Wolverine, Control Resonant and others all launched up against each other in September. NBA 2K27 was officially released globally on September 4, 2026.

Based on Zelnick's comments, GTA 6 won't just have affected NBA 2K27 sales, but caused some gamers to skip other games in favor of Rockstar's next, which comes out November 19. It is expected to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time, setting sales and revenue records, so Take-Two will of course be fine for some time to come. Other publishers and developers, though, might be left struggling.

For now, though, during the quarter Take-Two saw revenue of $1.6 billion, which was slightly below its guidance range of $1.62-$1.67 billion. The company said fiscal 2027 will be "an historic year for Take-Two – driven by our unwavering commitment to delivering the highest quality entertainment experiences." It reiterated our Fiscal 2027 outlook for revenue of $8-$8.2 billion.

Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

articles.title: Happy Mask Shopkeeper - All Happy Mask Sales - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Happy Mask Shopkeeper is a Thread of Light sidequest in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. This quest involves buying and selling four different
articles.body:
Happy Mask Shopkeeper is a Thread of Light sidequest in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. This quest involves buying and selling four different Masks on behalf of the Happy Mask Shop in Castle Town. The reward for this quest is mostly Rupees, but also access to various Masks that change NPC interactions across the game.

See IGN's complete guide to Happy Mask Shopkeeper below.

This Thread of Light can be started after you show Zelda's Letter to the hate guard in Kakariko Village. Better yet, our first sale target is that same NPC, who tips you off to the Happy Mask Shop and asks you if you could get him the Keaton Mask.

Return to Castle Town and the Happy Mask Shop. After speaking to the Happy Mask Shopkeeper and exhausting his dialogue, check out the Keaton Mask which is the only option at this time.

Return to the gate guard in Kakariko Village and he will buy the mask from you for 15 Rupees. Return to the Happy Mask Shop and pay for the mask, 10 Rupees, leaving you with a profit of 5 Rupees.

Next up is the Skull Mask . Speaking to the bearded man outside the Happy Mask Shop will provide a small hint, he says that someone in the forest might like this mask.

Head to the Lost Woods, then immediately go left from the entrance to find Skull Kid. True to his namesake, he wants the Skull Mask. He pays you 10 Rupees for it, which means a net loss of 10 Rupees once you return to the Happy Mask Shopkeeper.

Next check out the Spooky Mask . Speak to the bearded man outside the Shop and he suggests a kid who hangs out in dark and spooky places might enjoy this mask.

Head to the Kakariko Village Graveyard during the day where you will find a young boy stalking the grounds, emulating Dampe. He wants the Spooky Mask, and pays 50 Rupees for it. This nets us a profit of 20 Rupees, meaning we are back in the black overall!

Finally we will check out the Bunny Hood . The bearded man outside the shop suggests you offer it to someone who loves running through the fields.

Exit Castle Town into Hyrule Field and begin wandering around until you see the Running Man.

If you are having trouble, find a high spot to stand on so you can see more of the field (if you wait until night, you can find him sitting by the boulder northwest of Kokiri Forest).

He will freeze in his tracks when he sees you wearing the Bunny Hood. Speak to him and he will buy it from you for a whopping 200 Rupees! Make sure you've got some space in your Wallet.

Return to the Happy Mask Shop and pay 50 Rupees for the Bunny Hood. This completes the sidequest, and your reward is access to four more Masks: the Mask of Truth, Goron Mask, Zora Mask, and Gerudo Mask.

The Mask of Truth is the grand prize here. Wearing it allows you to read the thoughts of NPCs all over the game .

It also allows you to speak to the Gossip Stones, which offer tips and tricks.

Up Next: How to Get the Biggoron Sword - Trading Sidequest
